title: と思います : I Think That

blocks.content: **と思います** expresses personal opinion or belief. The と marks the boundary of the thought being reported. It makes statements sound appropriately tentative : stating something flatly without it can feel blunt.

lines: [Plain form verb / い-adj] + **と思います**   ← I think that ~

rows.japanese: 明日は雨が降ると思います。
rows.romaji: Ashita wa ame ga furu to omoimasu.
rows.english: I think it will rain tomorrow.

rows.japanese: 彼は来ないと思います。
この映画は面白いと思います。
rows.romaji: Kono eiga wa omoshiroi to omoimasu.
rows.english: I think this movie is interesting.

rows.japanese: もう少し考えたほうがいいと思います。
rows.romaji: Mō sukoshi kangaeta hō ga ii to omoimasu.
rows.english: I think you should think it over a bit more.

blocks.content: The clause before と is always in the **plain form**, not the polite form. 来ます**と**思います is wrong : it should be 来る**と**思います. The politeness is carried by the final と思います alone.
